newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Exiled king makes second visit to Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Exiled king makes second visit to Bulgaria.

text.p: Exiled King Simeon arrived in northern Bulgaria on Tuesday to a rapturous welcome on his second visit to the homeland he fled as a child in 1946.
Simeon flew into an airfield near the town of Veliko Tarnovo, where he will attend a ceremony marking the anniversary of Bulgaria's first constitution.
Some 3,000 people waving national and monarchist flags and portraits of the king surrounded him, chanting "Long Live Simeon" as he walked to his open-topped car.
Bulgaria holds parliamentary elections on Saturday and two coalitions are fighting for the support of monarchist parties.

"I have come to say personally what I think because people have interpreted my thoughts differently," the balding, bearded monarch said in brief remarks at the airport, adding that he would clarify his position later.

Simeon's aides insist he is the king of all Bulgarians and does not favour any one group, but Bulgaria's main monarchist parties have formed an alliance with the ethnic Turkish Movement for Rights and Freedoms (MRF).
Simeon received their leaders at his home in Madrid last week and pictures of them together now appear on the coalition's election posters.

Other monarchist movements are allied with the Union of Democratic Forces, which is expected to win a majority in Saturday's elections and is seen as more sympathetic to the monarchist cause than the previous Socialist administration.
"Your Majesty, you are always welcome in your homeland," said Marius Donkin, spokesman of the United Monarchist Party, greeting him at the airport.

Police said the chartered plane had flown low over the snow-covered mountains before landing so Simeon could see the homeland he left as a child of nine after the Soviet Army installed a puppet communist regime.
He returned to Bulgaria for the first time for a three-week visit in May last year.
At the height of demonstrations against the former Socialist government in January, he added his voice to calls for early parliamentary elections as a way out of the crisis.

"The King is in no position to influence Bulgarian politics directly but he can always show his support for a particular political force or political trend," MRF leader Ahmed Dogan told Reuters at the airport.
The 1879 Tarnovo constitution, which marks its 118th anniversary this week, was the first to be drawn up in the newly independent state after 500 years of Ottoman rule.
After addressing Tuesday's ceremony, the King was staying overnight at the mountain village of Arbanassy in a residence built and used by former communist dictator Todor Zhivkov.
On Wednesday, he will fly to Sofia for lunch with President Petar Stoyanov before returning to Madrid.
Simeon has never renounced his claim to the throne. As a Saxe-Coburg, he is related to other European royal families, including Britain's House of Windsor.
